slides.headline: Big toe stiff when you push off?
slides.sub: A stiff big toe is common, and there's plenty you can do about it.

slides.title: Why the big toe matters
slides.body: Every step, your big toe bends as you roll through to push off. When that joint gets stiff and sore, walking, running, squatting and rising onto your toes can all feel harder than usual.

slides.title: What's usually going on
slides.body: Hallux rigidus is a common arthritis-related stiffening of the big toe joint, sometimes with a bony bump on top. It tends to build over years, and symptoms usually go up and down with load.

slides.title: Shoes can take the load off
slides.body: A stiffer sole or a gentle rocker shape lets you roll through without bending the toe as much. Thongs and very bendy sneakers often feel worse, which is handy to know heading into summer.

slides.title: Keep the foot strong
slides.body: Calf raises within a comfortable range, toe and arch exercises, and general leg strength can help you walk with less strain on the joint. Your physio can adjust the range and volume as it settles.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: A toe that's hot, red and very swollen, pain that wakes you at night, numbness, or a sudden change after an injury are worth an assessment rather than waiting it out.

Hallux rigidus is a common stiffening of the big toe joint that tends to build over years. It can make walking, running and squatting feel harder, and flare-ups usually track with load.

Footwear is often the quickest win. A stiffer or gently rocker-shaped sole means the toe bends less with each step, while thongs and very bendy sneakers can make it grumpier. Calf and foot strengthening helps you share the load.
